stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drive a real battery through a variable load. Move each slider — $E$ (e.m.f.), $r$ (internal resistance), $R$ (load) — and watch how $U$, $I$ and the U(I) line respond.
stages.concept: A real generator obeys $U = E - r\cdot I$: its terminal voltage $U$ drops linearly with the current $I$ it delivers, at a rate set by its internal resistance $r$. The intercept is $E$, the slope is $-r$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: The dashed line shows a target characteristic. Adjust $E$ and $r$ (the load $R$ only moves the operating point along the line — it does not change the line itself) so your solid line matches the target. Two targets, ±5%.
stages.concept: Two batteries share the same characteristic only if they share both $E$ and $r$. Reading a characteristic: $y$-intercept is $E$, slope is $-r$, and $x$-intercept is the short-circuit current $I_{cc} = E/r$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: A sealed generator hides $E$ and $r$. The characteristic is off. Set the load $R$ to any value, read the meters, note $(U, I)$. Repeat at a different $R$. Deduce $E$ and $r$ on paper, then enter both. 3 attempts per battery; three batteries in a row.
stages.concept: Two operating points on the same line pin it down. From $(U_1, I_1)$ and $(U_2, I_2)$: $r = (U_1 - U_2) / (I_2 - I_1)$, then $E = U_1 + r \cdot I_1$.

labels.measure_pending: — set R and read the meters
labels.tip1: each slider sweeps a different piece of the physics — try short-circuit (R small) and open-circuit (R large) too
labels.tip2: E sets where the line hits the U-axis; r sets how steeply it falls with I
labels.tip3: read (U, I) at two different R values — then solve on paper before typing
labels.peek_tip: The generator's line is $U = E - r\cdot I$. Two operating points fix it: $r = (U_1 - U_2)/(I_2 - I_1)$, then $E = U_1 + r\cdot I_1$.

1.1: Try pushing R all the way down (near short-circuit) and all the way up (near open-circuit). Watch U and I swap roles.
1.2: At open-circuit (R very large), I is tiny and U is close to E. At short-circuit (R very small), U is close to 0 and I peaks at about E/r.
1.3: Move E: the whole line shifts up/down. Move r: the line tilts. Move R: only the dot slides along a fixed line.

2.1: The dashed line's y-intercept is the target E. Its slope (rise/run) is minus the target r. Read those off before touching sliders.
2.2: Match the y-intercept first with E, then adjust r so the two lines overlap. R does not matter for this stage.
2.3: ±5% tolerance means the numbers don't need to be exact. Get within a slider step of each target and the tick fires.

3.1: Set R to any value in the low half of its range. Note U and I. Then set R higher and note U and I again. Two points fix a line.
3.2: Slope = (U₂ − U₁) / (I₂ − I₁). Because U falls as I rises, that slope is negative, and r is its absolute value.
3.3: Once r is known, plug either point into U = E − r·I and solve for E. Then type both and submit.
